analysis.title: Precious under pressure
key_insights: Precious metals have been under sustained pressure since late August, when gold briefly broke above its 200-day SMA, failed, and reversed sharply lower to retest support around USD 3,950, in line with the June and July cyclical lows.

The weakness runs against the usual macro correlation: the complex fell as Treasury yields rose, and a pause in yield gains did not bring support to safe-haven assets. Pictet points to broader liquidation flows, a possible unwind of the geopolitical risk premium and a stronger US dollar.

Flows: cumulative flows into developed-market precious metals funds and ETFs have been dominated by outflows over the past seven months since the January price peak. Recent data show the gauge recovering from negative territory, meaning outflows are moderating. If sustained, this could mean better flow momentum and a somewhat more constructive technical backdrop in the coming weeks.

Gold hit an all-time high near 5,600 at the start of the year after a parabolic run. It has since fallen below its 200-day SMA for the first time since November 2023, which confirms a broader consolidation phase.

Gold's long-term bullish structure remains intact while medium-term support at 3,880-3,950 holds. A break below would weaken it and could open the way to 3,330-3,500, the long-term trend support area (50% Fibonacci retracement and former horizontal resistance).

Gold's short-term picture is strained: RSI broke below its support line, showing fading upside momentum. While gold stays below the short-term risk area at 4,170-4,280, a break of 3,880-3,950 cannot be ruled out.

GDX broke above its 2011 all-time high of 67 last September, completed a wave-3 at 117 (261.8% Fibonacci extension), then corrected to the 67-69 area (50% retracement). It rebounded, reclaimed the 200-day SMA, failed at the 76.4% retracement of the prior decline and has pulled back toward 78, suggesting a developing triangle.

GDX: holding 78 keeps the triangle valid with scope for a recovery above 85-89, and a break above 85-89 could validate a move to 99. Below 78 the triangle fails and the focus shifts to the 58-55 long-term support area. RSI broke below support.

Silver broke the 55 resistance that had capped prices since 1979, rose to an all-time high of 122, then consolidated back to the 55-50 former breakout area. It is holding above this zone, with key support at 50 (former 1979 resistance and 76.4% Fibonacci retracement).

Platinum failed at the 1,915-1,930 risk area (200-day SMA, previous local high and falling resistance in place since January 2026) and is testing key support at 1,550 with the momentum indicator negative. Below the falling resistance, which coincides with the 50-day SMA at 1,748, downside could extend to 1,350-1,250 (76.4% retracement, near the 200-week SMA). A break above 1,748 would improve the picture and allow a recovery toward 1,915-1,930.

Palladium failed at 2,220 (50% retracement of the prior down leg), completed a head and shoulders pattern and broke below both the 200-week SMA and the 76.4% retracement. The pattern's downside target is near 870. RSI has turned lower.
Pictet frames the setup as a consolidation within a secular uptrend if current levels hold, citing stabilizing fund flows. Vulnerability is greater in platinum and palladium than in gold and silver.

Macro read: persistently high real Treasury yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets and pressure valuations. For the secular uptrend to hold, the case may need to rely less on the inflation-hedge narrative and more on hedging sovereign credit and fiscal risk, with central bank demand as structural support.

sector_views.rationale: Long-term uptrends in gold and silver are intact above 3,880-3,950 and 50-55, but short-term momentum has weakened and platinum and palladium are technically weaker.

tension_points.bull_case: Gold and silver hold major historical support (3,880-3,950 and 50-55), outflows from precious metals funds are moderating, and the secular uptrend could resume with central bank demand as structural support.
tension_points.bear_case: Momentum is fading with RSI breaking support, real yields stay high, a stronger dollar and liquidation flows weigh on prices, and platinum and palladium are breaking down technically.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below gold's 3,880-3,950 support zone, which could open 3,330-3,500.
